Hi Rajesh / Samantha -

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we have alignment before the network/infrastructure deep-dive: 

Summary of performance targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 120ms for streaming responses (token-by-token streaming)
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec for user-facing inference flows; each request may open up to 4 concurrent streaming connections for multi-stream sessions
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrency ~500 simultaneous sessions across two clusters
- Streaming requirements: low idle keepalive (HTTP/2 or websocket), partial-response behavior preserved (server-side chunking)

Operational notes that matter for Private/VPC deployment:
- We recommend pinning model variants for predictable latency. Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix-caching which will reduce per-token latency but requires stable routing and sticky sessions for cache locality.
- Batch sizing: we'll tune batching but need worst-case single-request path to meet the p95 above.

Network qualification items / asks for your team (next steps):
1) Provide network topology (diagram) showing where Redwood Private will be reachable (VPN endpoint or VPC peering), and whether TLS termination happens in your perimeter or at our side.
2) Confirm whether you prefer IPsec VPN or cloud provider peering (ExpressRoute/Direct Connect). If peering, provide account IDs and expected cross-region routing.
3) Confirm egress/NAT behavior and whether we should expect source NAT; provide public IP ranges if applicable.
4) Share intended subnets and any firewalls (port/ACL) between app layer and inference VPC.
5) Run a quick iperf3 test between your app hosts and the target VPC subnet (we've attached a small template for results). Target internal latency budget: <= 20ms between app and inference hosts to comfortably meet the p95 token latency.

Attachments: SLO_worksheet.xlsx (filled template you can use), network_req_template.pdf (network checklist).

Proposed next steps:
- You run the iperf and send results + topology (attachment) - target EOD Thursday 7/29.
- Schedule a technical walkthrough (30-45m) with your network/infrastructure team and our infra engs - proposed Monday 8/02 10:00 AM PT.
- We'll prepare a draft MPA for procurement review (sending initial version this thread).

If any of the targets above need to shift (eg higher throughput or lower latency) flag that and we will run a quick perf modeling exercise.

Thanks -

Samantha - thanks, the topology looks good and the ExpressRoute approach makes sense. Quick answers to your infra questions: 

1) HTTP/2: yes, our runtime supports HTTP/2 multiplexing and gRPC streams; we also support websocket-based streaming if your LB prefers. Multiplexing is fine but for KV cache locality we recommend a small set of stable upstream connections (stickiness) so the same worker sees repeat prefixes - in practice a 5-15 minute session affinity window works well.

2) Keepalives / TCP tuning: we recommend setting idle keepalive > 90s for long-lived streams to avoid premature LB timeouts. TCP settings: enable TCP_USER_TIMEOUT tuning if available; increase max_syn_backlog and ensure BDP-based window scaling (standard cloud defaults are usually okay). We'll share a short tuning doc after the call.

For the point about TLS/mTLS: we can support mTLS with customer-managed CAs; for Private deployments customers typically terminate TLS at their ALB and use mTLS for inter-VPC auth if they want zero-trust on the wire. If you prefer Redwood to terminate TLS inside the Private VPC, we can discuss certificate options and KMS integration (customer-managed KMS is supported).

I attached a draft MPA for procurement to start reviewing; Neha, can you coordinate with procurement on redlines?
